description: Construct a complete GPT-like transformer language model from first principles: BPE tokenization, multi-head self-attention, layer normalization, residual connections, and autoregressive text generation.

steps.title: Text Tokenization & Positional Embeddings
steps.objective: Convert raw string corpora into discrete integer token sequences and add positional vector encodings.
steps.whyNecessary: Neural networks process numerical tensor matrices, not character strings. Positional embeddings encode the word order since attention is order-agnostic.
steps.content: Build a dataset loader that slides a context window over tokens. Map input tokens to d_model dimensional vectors using nn.Embedding. Add learned absolute positional embeddings.
steps.expectedResult: Text 'Hello world' turns into tensors `[15496, 995]` with shape `[1, 2, 768]`.

steps.title: Causal Scaled Dot-Product Self-Attention
steps.objective: Implement the attention equation: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V with future masking.
steps.whyNecessary: Self-attention allows every token to query and weigh contextual information from preceding tokens while masking prevents looking ahead.
steps.content: Compute Queries, Keys, and Values through linear projection. Calculate attention score matrix. Apply an upper-triangular mask of negative infinity (-inf) before softmax.
steps.expectedResult: Attention matrix shape `[seq_len, seq_len]` properly zeros out upper right probabilities.

steps.title: Multi-Head Attention & Transformer Block
steps.objective: Split embedding dimension across multiple attention heads and encapsulate inside a residual TransformerBlock.
steps.whyNecessary: Multiple heads allow the model to attend jointly to information from different representation subspaces (e.g. grammar vs semantics).
steps.content: Implement `MultiHeadAttention` with `num_heads`. Wrap with LayerNorm and FeedForward network (GELU activation) with residual skip connections (`x + sublayer(x)`).
steps.codeSnippet:
class TransformerBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.attn = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.ffn = FeedForward(d_model)
    def forward(self, x):
        x = x + self.attn(self.ln1(x))
        x = x + self.ffn(self.ln2(x))
        return x
steps.expectedResult: Tensors flow through 12 stacked transformer blocks maintaining gradient stability.

steps.title: Autoregressive Text Generation & Sampling
steps.objective: Sample next tokens iteratively given a starting prompt using temperature and top-k filtering.
steps.whyNecessary: Raw argmax sampling produces repetitive and boring output; temperature-scaled sampling produces creative and natural completions.
steps.content: Predict logits for next token. Divide logits by `temperature`. Filter to top `k` candidates. Sample from resulting multinomial distribution and append to input sequence.
steps.codeSnippet:
def generate_text(model, idx, max_new_tokens, temperature=0.8, top_k=50):
    for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
        logits = model(idx[:, -max_len:])[:, -1, :] / temperature
        v, _ = torch.topk(logits, min(top_k, logits.size(-1)))
        logits[logits < v[:, [-1]]] = -float('Inf')
        probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        idx_next = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
        idx = torch.cat((idx, idx_next), dim=1)
    return idx
steps.expectedResult: Prompt 'In a distant galaxy' generates 50 coherent continuation tokens.

title: Build Your Own Container Using Less Than 100 Lines of Go
description: Understand Linux containerization from first principles by creating an isolated process runtime using Linux namespaces, cgroups, chroot, and syscalls in Go.

steps.title: Fork and Execute Arbitrary Commands
steps.objective: Build the baseline runner using os/exec that takes arguments and executes them via exec.Command.
steps.whyNecessary: Container runtimes start by executing an entrypoint process on behalf of the user.
steps.content: Implement `main()` parsing `run <command> <args>`. Use `exec.Command(os.Args[2], os.Args[3:]...)` and bind Stdin, Stdout, and Stderr to the terminal.
steps.expectedResult: 'go run main.go run echo hello' prints 'hello' to stdout.

steps.title: Isolate Hostname with UTS Namespace
steps.objective: Provide the container its own distinct hostname using Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS.
steps.whyNecessary: UTS (UNIX Timesharing System) namespace prevents changes to the container hostname from affecting the host machine.
steps.content: Attach `SysProcAttr` with `CLONE_NEWUTS`. Inside the child process, call `syscall.Sethostname([]byte("container"))`.
steps.expectedResult: Changing hostname inside the container to 'my-box' does not modify the host's hostname.

steps.title: Isolate Process Tree with PID Namespace
steps.objective: Make the container's entrypoint process believe it is PID 1 using CLONE_NEWPID.
steps.whyNecessary: In Linux, PID 1 is the init system. Isolate the process tree so the container cannot inspect or terminate host processes.
steps.content: Because PID namespace only takes effect on child processes, re-execute the program binary (`/proc/self/exe child <args>`) with `CLONE_NEWPID` enabled.
steps.expectedResult: 'ps' inside the container only displays processes spawned within the container.

steps.title: Filesystem Sandboxing with chroot & Mounts
steps.objective: Confine the container to a dedicated root filesystem directory and mount a private procfs.
steps.whyNecessary: Without filesystem isolation, the container can read and modify sensitive host files like /etc/passwd or /root.
steps.content: Download an Alpine Linux rootfs. In the child process, call `syscall.Chroot("/path/to/rootfs")`, `os.Chdir("/")`, and mount procfs using `syscall.Mount("proc", "/proc", "proc", 0, "")`.
steps.codeSnippet:
syscall.Chroot("/path/to/rootfs")
os.Chdir("/")
syscall.Mount("proc", "/proc", "proc", 0, "")
steps.expectedResult: Running 'ls /' inside container reveals only the Alpine rootfs files.

steps.title: Resource Restrictions with cgroups v2
steps.objective: Limit the container's memory consumption to 100MB and cap max pids to prevent fork bombs.
steps.whyNecessary: Control groups (cgroups) prevent a single buggy or malicious container from consuming all host RAM and crashing the server.
steps.content: Create a new cgroup directory under `/sys/fs/cgroup/flowctrl/`. Write `100M` to `memory.max` and `20` to `pids.max`. Append the child process PID to `cgroup.procs`.
steps.codeSnippet:
os.WriteFile("/sys/fs/cgroup/flowctrl/memory.max", []byte("100M"), 0700)
os.WriteFile("/sys/fs/cgroup/flowctrl/cgroup.procs", []byte(strconv.Itoa(os.Getpid())), 0700)
steps.expectedResult: A memory-leaking process inside the container is killed by the OOM killer when hitting 100MB without affecting the host.

steps.objective: Implement render() to recursively convert Virtual DOM nodes into real browser DOM elements.
steps.whyNecessary: Understanding basic recursive rendering reveals why deep trees freeze the browser without Fiber.
steps.content: Create elements with `document.createElement(fiber.type)`. Assign props and event listeners. Recursively call `render()` on all children.

steps.title: Concurrent Work Loop & Fiber Node Structure
steps.objective: Break rendering into atomic units of work using requestIdleCallback and a Fiber linked list.
steps.whyNecessary: If the component tree is huge, recursive rendering blocks the main thread. A cooperative work loop yields to user input and animations.
steps.content: Structure each Fiber node with `child`, `sibling`, and `parent` pointers. Write `workLoop(deadline)` that executes units of work until time expires, then yields back to the browser.
steps.expectedResult: Complex UI rendering no longer drops 60 FPS animation frames.

steps.title: Fiber Tree Reconciliation & Commit Phase
steps.objective: Compare previous fibers with new elements to generate UPDATE, PLACEMENT, and DELETION tags, then commit mutations in one batch.
steps.whyNecessary: Mutating the real DOM piece-by-piece causes visual stutter and layout thrashing. Calculating diffs first and committing all at once ensures smooth updates.
steps.content: In `reconcileChildren`, compare `oldFiber.type` with `newElement.type`. If identical, reuse DOM node with `UPDATE` tag. If different, create new node with `PLACEMENT` tag and schedule old node with `DELETION`. Commit all DOM updates in `commitRoot()`.

steps.whyNecessary: Modern React relies on functional components and hooks for clean state management.

steps.title: Set Up Socket Server & Non-Blocking Sockets
steps.objective: Initialize a TCP listener socket on port 6379 and configure it for non-blocking I/O using fcntl.
steps.whyNecessary: Blocking sockets cause a server to halt while waiting for one client, freezing all other connected clients.
steps.content: Call socket(), bind() to 0.0.0.0:6379, and listen(). Use fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, O_NONBLOCK) on the listening socket and every newly accepted client connection.
steps.expectedResult: Server boots on port 6379 and accepts connections via netcat or telnet without blocking.

steps.title: The Event Loop with poll() / epoll()
steps.objective: Manage hundreds of concurrent connections using an event multiplexer.
steps.whyNecessary: An event loop lets a single thread monitor multiple sockets, only waking up when data is ready to be read or written.
steps.content: Maintain a dynamic vector of struct pollfd. Add the server socket with POLLIN to accept incoming connections. Add active client sockets with POLLIN to read data. Remove closed sockets to prevent fd leaks.
steps.expectedResult: Multiple simultaneous netcat connections can connect without hanging the server.

steps.title: Parse the Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP)
steps.objective:
Parse array-of-bulk-strings command framing: '*<count>
$<len>
<data>
'.
steps.whyNecessary: RESP is binary-safe and allows Redis to handle keys and values containing any byte, including null terminators and newlines.
steps.content: Implement a zero-copy buffer scanner. Detect message boundaries marked by CRLF (\r\n). Parse bulk strings by length header to avoid scanning payload bytes.
steps.expectedResult: Executing 'redis-cli -p 6379 PING' parses correctly and responds with '+PONG\r\n'.

steps.title: Implement the In-Memory Key-Value Hashtable
steps.objective: Build an efficient hashtable to store string keys and values with constant time O(1) lookups.
steps.whyNecessary: Redis's primary value proposition is sub-millisecond key-value retrieval from RAM.
steps.content: Implement chaining collision resolution with MurmurHash3 or SipHash. Implement progressive resizing (two internal tables) so resizing is distributed over successive queries without freezing the server.
steps.expectedResult:
'SET key val' returns '+OK
', and 'GET key' returns '$3
val
'.

steps.title: Key Expiration & TTL Management
steps.objective: Implement EXPIRE, TTL, and automatic background eviction of stale keys.
steps.whyNecessary: Without TTL expiration, in-memory caches quickly exhaust available RAM and crash.
steps.content: Maintain a secondary hashtable or min-heap mapping keys to expiration timestamps (millisecond epoch). On each event loop tick, sample 20 keys with TTLs and purge expired ones.
steps.expectedResult: Keys set with 'EXPIRE mykey 2' disappear from GET requests after exactly 2 seconds.

title: Build Your Own SQLite Database from Scratch
description: Build a lightweight relational database inspired by SQLite, featuring a REPL front-end, bytecode compiler, in-memory paging, and B-Tree disk persistence.

steps.title: Design the Interactive REPL & Input Buffer
steps.objective: Create the Read-Eval-Print Loop that accepts commands, handles buffer resizing, and parses meta-commands like .exit.
steps.whyNecessary: All database systems require a client interface to accept query strings from users or socket connections.
steps.content: Implement an InputBuffer struct that wraps getline() to dynamically allocate memory as the user types commands. Intercept meta-commands beginning with a dot ('.exit') to cleanly exit the REPL without executing SQL parser routines.
steps.expectedResult: Running the executable outputs 'db > ' prompt. Typing '.exit' terminates the process with code 0.

steps.title: Implement the SQL Tokenizer & Prepared Statement Parser
steps.objective: Convert raw input text into strongly-typed Statement structs (STATEMENT_INSERT, STATEMENT_SELECT).
steps.whyNecessary: Separating query parsing from execution prevents SQL injection and prepares commands for the virtual machine.
steps.content: Build a prepare_statement() function that inspects the first token. For 'insert', parse arguments using sscanf() into a Row struct (id, username, email). Validate string lengths to protect against buffer overflows.
steps.expectedResult: Commands like 'insert 1 user user@example.com' are recognized and stored in the statement object.

steps.title: Define the Row Layout & In-Memory Pager
steps.objective: Design a compact binary memory layout for rows and group rows into fixed 4096-byte pages.
steps.whyNecessary: Databases organize memory in fixed-size blocks (pages) matching operating system page sizes to minimize disk fragmentation and maximize I/O throughput.
steps.content: Define COLUMN_USERNAME_SIZE (32) and COLUMN_EMAIL_SIZE (255). Serialize rows into contiguous bytes within pages. Create a Table struct holding an array of 100 page pointers that are allocated on demand.
steps.expectedResult: Multiple rows can be inserted and retrieved from contiguous memory pages without corruption.

steps.title: Disk Persistence & Flushing with Paged I/O
steps.objective: Save all cached memory pages to a persistent file when the database closes, and reload them on boot.
steps.whyNecessary: Without persistence, data is lost when the database process exits.
steps.content: Open a file descriptor using open() with O_RDWR | O_CREAT flags. On db_open(), read the file size to calculate row counts. On db_close(), iterate through allocated pages and write() them sequentially before freeing memory.
steps.expectedResult: Inserting 10 rows, exiting the database, and restarting it preserves all 10 rows on SELECT.

steps.title: B-Tree Node Architecture & Leaf Node Layout
steps.objective: Replace the flat array storage with a B-Tree leaf node format capable of sorting keys.
steps.whyNecessary: A flat array requires O(N) linear scans to find a record. A B-Tree enables O(log N) searches and range queries.
steps.content: Define header fields in each 4KB leaf node: is_root, parent_pointer, num_cells. Each cell stores a uint32_t key followed by the serialized Row value. Keep cells sorted by key to enable binary search.
steps.expectedResult: Keys are inserted in sorted order, enabling binary searching within leaf nodes in logarithmic time.

steps.title: B-Tree Node Splitting & Multi-Level Trees
steps.objective: Implement leaf node splitting and internal routing nodes when a page exceeds 4096 bytes.
steps.whyNecessary: When a leaf node is full, the tree must split into two sibling nodes and create an internal parent node to maintain logarithmic depth.
steps.content: When leaf_node_num_cells reaches max capacity, allocate a new page. Copy the upper half of cells into the sibling page. Create or update an internal node storing child page numbers and pivot keys. Update the root pointer.
steps.expectedResult: The database seamlessly handles inserting 10,000+ rows, automatically growing tree depth.

steps.title: Enter Terminal Raw Mode
steps.objective: Disable canonical mode and echo so keypresses are read immediately byte-by-byte without waiting for Enter.
steps.whyNecessary: By default, terminals wait for the Enter key before sending input to the program, which is incompatible with interactive text editors.
steps.content: Use `tcgetattr` and `tcsetattr` from `<termios.h>`. Disable `ECHO`, `ICANON`, `ISIG`, and `IXON` flags. Register `disableRawMode()` via `atexit()` to ensure the terminal resets on exit.
steps.expectedResult: Pressing keys prints their ASCII values immediately without echoing or waiting for Enter.

steps.title: Clear Screen & Position Cursor with Escape Sequences
steps.objective: Use standard VT100 escape sequences to clear the screen and draw the tilde '~' margin.
steps.whyNecessary: Escape sequences allow programs to control colors, clear screens, and position cursors across all standard terminals.
steps.content: Write `\x1b[2J` to clear the screen, and `\x1b[H` to move the cursor to row 1, col 1. Draw a column of tildes (`~`) on empty rows just like Vim.
steps.expectedResult: Terminal clears completely and displays a Vim-like '~' gutter.

steps.title: Row Representation & File Loading
steps.objective: Read text files from disk into an array of `erow` structs containing string characters and rendered tabs.
steps.whyNecessary: The editor must hold all file rows in memory to enable scrolling and modification.
steps.content: Implement `editorOpen(char *filename)`. Use `getline()` in a loop to read lines into `E.row[E.numrows]`. Convert tab characters (`\t`) into spaces for consistent rendering.
steps.expectedResult: './kilo main.c' loads and displays the source code cleanly.

steps.title: Arrow Key Navigation & Screen Scrolling
steps.objective: Parse multi-byte arrow escape sequences ('\x1b[A', etc.) and scroll when the cursor moves off screen.
steps.whyNecessary: Files are typically longer than the terminal window height and wider than its width.
steps.content: Maintain `rowoff` and `coloff` offsets. If cursor row `E.cy` < `E.rowoff`, scroll up; if `E.cy` >= `E.rowoff + E.screenrows`, scroll down.
steps.expectedResult: Navigating with arrow keys smoothly scrolls through thousand-line files.

steps.title: Text Editing & File Saving
steps.objective: Implement character insertion, backspace deletion, and save changes back to disk with Ctrl-S.
steps.whyNecessary: An editor must allow interactive modifications and persist work to storage.
steps.content: On standard character input, call `editorRowInsertChar()`. On backspace, shift trailing characters left. On Ctrl-S, write the buffer to disk using `open()` with `O_RDWR | O_CREAT`.
steps.expectedResult: Typing inserts letters at cursor position; pressing Ctrl-S saves the updated file.

title: Write Yourself a Git! (Content-Addressable Storage)
description: Build a complete Git client from scratch in Python, implementing content-addressable storage, blob/tree/commit objects, zlib compression, and repository staging.

steps.title: Initialize the .git Directory Hierarchy
steps.objective: Create the standard repository structure: .git/objects, .git/refs/heads, and .git/HEAD.
steps.whyNecessary: Every Git repository is governed by standard file locations that store configuration, branches, and object databases.
steps.content: Implement `init [path]` command. Create directories `.git/objects/`, `.git/refs/heads/`, and `.git/refs/tags/`. Create `.git/HEAD` containing 'ref: refs/heads/master\n' and `.git/config` with basic repository configuration.
steps.codeSnippet:
import os

def repo_create(path):
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(path, ".git", "objects"), exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(path, ".git", "refs", "heads"), exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(path, ".git", "HEAD"), "w") as f:
        f.write("ref: refs/heads/master\n")
steps.expectedResult: Running 'mygit init' generates a directory that the official 'git status' recognizes as a valid repository.

steps.title: The Object Database & Blob Storage
steps.objective: Hash files using SHA-1, prepend the object header, compress with zlib, and store under .git/objects/xx/yyyy...
steps.whyNecessary: Content-addressability means files with identical content share the exact same hash, preventing duplicate storage.
steps.content: Git objects follow the format: `<type> <length>\x00<data>`. Compute `hash = sha1(formatted_bytes)`. The first 2 characters form the subfolder inside `.git/objects/`, and the remaining 38 form the filename.
steps.codeSnippet:
import hashlib, zlib

def object_write(data, type_name="blob"):
    header = f"{type_name} {len(data)}\x00".encode()
    full_content = header + data
    sha = hashlib.sha1(full_content).hexdigest()
    path = os.path.join(".git", "objects", sha[:2], sha[2:])
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(zlib.compress(full_content))
    return sha
steps.expectedResult: Writing 'hello world' produces hash `3b18e512dba79e4c8300dd08aeb37f8e728b8dad` exactly matching `git hash-object`.

steps.title: Read Objects with 'cat-file'
steps.objective: Decompress an object from disk using its SHA-1 hash, verify the header, and display its contents.
steps.whyNecessary: Reading objects is required to inspect history, view previous file revisions, and check out commits.
steps.content: Read the file at `.git/objects/{sha[:2]}/{sha[2:]}`, decompress using `zlib.decompress()`, split at the null byte `\x00` to extract type and length, and return the payload.
steps.codeSnippet:
def object_read(sha):
    path = os.path.join(".git", "objects", sha[:2], sha[2:])
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        raw = zlib.decompress(f.read())
    null_idx = raw.find(b'\x00')
    header = raw[:null_idx].decode()
    type_name, size = header.split()
    return type_name, raw[null_idx+1:]
steps.expectedResult: 'mygit cat-file -p <hash>' prints the original file contents to stdout.

steps.title: Tree Objects (Directories & Permissions)
steps.objective: Serialize folder structures into Git tree objects containing file permissions, names, and SHA-1 hashes.
steps.whyNecessary: While blobs store file contents, trees store filenames, directory structures, and UNIX file permissions (100644 for files, 040000 for directories).
steps.content: Parse binary tree records: `<mode> <filename>\x00<binary_sha20>`. Implement `ls-tree` to list contents of a directory node recursively.
steps.codeSnippet:
def tree_parse_one(raw, start=0):
    space = raw.find(b' ', start)
    mode = raw[start:space]
    null = raw.find(b'\x00', space)
    name = raw[space+1:null].decode()
    sha = raw[null+1:null+21].hex()
    return null + 21, (mode, name, sha)
steps.expectedResult: 'mygit ls-tree <tree-hash>' prints all files and child folders in the tree.

steps.title: Commit Objects & Commit History Traversal
steps.objective: Create commit objects tying together a root tree, parent commit hash, author info, timestamp, and commit message.
steps.whyNecessary: Commits record snapshots of the tree at specific moments in time, creating the immutable ledger of software history.
steps.content:
Format commit objects: `tree <hash>
parent <hash>
author Name <email> timestamp tz
committer ...

Commit message
